component.name: OctoSnap
component.summary: Capture, annotate and record the screen

description.p: OctoSnap takes a screenshot the moment you ask for one. Pick an area, a window or a whole screen with a keyboard shortcut, and the capture lands in a small card in the corner of the screen, ready to copy, save, drag into another app, or open for annotation.
Everything a capture might need, without leaving the desktop:

ul.li: Area, window and full-screen capture, with a magnifier, a frozen-screen mode and the pointer in or out
An editor with arrows, shapes, text, counters, a spotlight, redaction, highlighter, crop and backgrounds
Scrolling capture that stitches a long page into one image
Text recognition that copies the words in any part of the screen, on your own computer
Screenshots pinned above other windows, and a history of recent captures
Screen recording to GIF, with a trimming editor
Pixel-art pets that live on the desktop if you want them, and keep out of every capture

description.p: OctoSnap needs its GNOME Shell extension, which draws the capture overlay and reads the screen. The app carries it and installs it the first time it starts, and it starts after you log out and back in.
What it asks of the system, and why:

ul.li: GNOME Shell and its extensions: to find its extension, turn it on, and change the settings kept with it
Its extension's own folder, among your extensions: to install the extension it carries, and to update it
Mutter's screen cast and PipeWire: to record the area you chose as a GIF
Mutter's display configuration: to know each screen's name and refresh rate
The session manager: for the Log Out button that loads a newly installed extension, which asks you first
Pictures and Videos: where screenshots and recordings are saved
The network: only to download a text-recognition language pack, when you ask for one

screenshot.caption: Annotate a capture with arrows, shapes, numbered steps, text and redaction
Pick an area, a window or the whole screen from one toolbar
Settings for what happens after each capture

description.p: OctoSnap now runs on GNOME 46 and 47, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS among them.

ul.li: The GNOME Shell extension installs and runs on GNOME 46 and 47, where it was refused before
The extension also loads on GNOME 48 and 49, which it already named but could not run on

description.p: The crop frame goes where it is pulled.

ul.li: An edge of the crop frame can be taken anywhere along it, and a corner anywhere on its bracket, where most of the frame used to move all of it
On a background, pulling the frame's top or left edge no longer starts a new frame in the margin, and pulling its right or bottom edge no longer moves the whole frame
An edge taken a little inside it moves with the pointer, without first jumping to it
A double-click while cropping no longer opens a label for typing

description.p: Cards come up sooner and move more smoothly.

ul.li: A card goes up without waiting for the screenshot to reach the clipboard, and its picture is read in the background
A dragged card shows the card's picture under the pointer, not the whole screenshot
A card that comes back, after it was closed or from a pin or the editor, springs in from the edge of the screen
A card's buttons fade in and out more gently, and a closed card goes more quickly
Cards that move to make room, or to close a gap, settle just past their place and back

description.p: The editor is easier to work in.

ul.li: The editor opens at the size of the screenshot, with an even border round it, and the Background and Layers panels make room for themselves
What is selected is outlined in orange along its own shape, with handles that show what they do, and a click or a right-click away lets go of it
Text is typed as it will look, its colour is the letters' own, and it can have a background colour; the dots on a label's sides set the width of its box
The pencil and the highlighter pick up their own strokes to move them
The tools always sit on one line, level with the window's buttons, and the buttons at the bottom are icons
One Esc closes All-In-One

description.p: Desktop pets of your own.

ul.li: A pet pack, a folder with a sheet of the pet's frames and a short description of them, adds a pet of your own beside the five, and OctoSnap's updates leave it where it is
Settings → Pets opens the folder, shows each pack's pet among the others, and says what to change in a pack it cannot read

description.p: Windows open where they belong, even the first time.

ul.li: A card, a pin, the history or a capture's controls that are slow to draw, as the first ones after installing can be, open where they belong, not in the middle of the screen

description.p: OctoSnap reads your captures for you, and the editor gains a magnifier, layers, Cut Out and vector export.

ul.li: Redact Sensitive Info covers the e-mail addresses, phone numbers, IBANs, card numbers, IP addresses, keys and passwords in a picture, in one step
Select Text in the Picture (Ctrl+Shift+T) selects the words in a capture to copy them, and opens its links and addresses
The capture history finds a capture by the words in it, and so does the Activities search
The magnifier (M) shows part of the picture enlarged, joined to it by a line
The Layers panel (F9) lists every mark, and reorders, hides and locks them
Cut Out (Shift+X) removes a band across or down the picture and closes the gap
Save As writes SVG and PDF, with the marks as vectors
A pencil stroke held still becomes a line, a rectangle or an ellipse. A pen's pressure sets the pencil's width, and two fingers pinch to zoom
Numbered badges renumber themselves, and badges and labels can point at something
Ctrl+? lists every shortcut
OctoSnap's icon offers each capture and the history, and Files opens pictures in OctoSnap
From a terminal, a capture can go to standard output and a picture come from standard input

On a background, a pixelation or a blur is made from the part of the picture it covers, not from beside it; a spotlight darkens all of a cropped picture; and at square corners a cropped picture no longer shows the rest of the capture around it

On a background, a picture you paste or drop lands on the picture, and one dropped at an edge joins it inside the background, which grows around both. The crop snaps to the picture's edges where you see them
A background added after a crop past the picture's edge goes around the whole crop, the room it made and what is on it included, and None leaves the crop as it was

description.p: OctoSnap updates itself.

ul.li: The Flatpak now comes from OctoSnap's own repository, where every release is signed, and updates from it: in Software, with flatpak update, or from OctoSnap

When a new release is out, OctoSnap says so once, and installs it from that notification, from Settings, or from Update OctoSnap in the top bar's menu. It then starts the new release in its own place as soon as none of its windows is open
A Flatpak installed from an earlier release's file does not update: uninstall it, which keeps your settings and history, and install it from the repository, as the README says
The repository says how to report a bug or a security issue, and how to contribute

description.p: Text recognition says where to get the library it runs on.

ul.li: OctoSnap built from source reads text with the system's ONNX Runtime. When it is missing, a read now names the package to install for your distribution, with a button to the instructions, where before it only named the library
Once ONNX Runtime is installed, the next read uses it. Before, OctoSnap only noticed it after you logged out and back in
ONNX Runtime is found where Fedora and openSUSE install it

description.p: Text recognition tells you what it needs, and gets it.

ul.li: Reading text with no language pack installed opens Settings at the language packs, with the one for your language ready to install. Once it is in, the text you captured is read and copied, with no need to capture it again
The Install and Remove buttons of the language packs work. Before, they did nothing, so a new installation could not get a pack from Settings
A text capture no longer plays the camera shutter or flies to the corner as a screenshot does: its sound is the one that says the text was copied

description.p: Quieter pets, aligned text, and a clipboard read from anywhere.

ul.li: Two new Liveliness settings for the pets: Silent, where they start nothing by themselves but still react to you, and Zen, far calmer than Calm. A new size, Smol, sits between Tiny and Small
Marks drawn on a background's margin are no longer cut away, and None in the Background panel takes the whole background away
Text can be aligned left, centred or right
The default background preset can be added to every new screenshot, from the editor's Presets menu or from Settings
A picture made from a saved project remembers it: the history's Projects filter finds it, and Annotate opens the project again
The unsaved-changes dot and a card's Trash button follow what was really saved, so undoing and drawing again is no longer taken for saved work
Annotate the Clipboard's Image works while another application has the keyboard, for a copied picture or a copied image file

description.p: Saved files are the format you chose, and a copied GIF stays animated.

ul.li: A screenshot saved as JPEG or WebP is now really a JPEG or a WebP, and the JPEG quality setting is used: before, both were PNG files under another name
Save As writes the format the name you give asks for
Copying a GIF copies the file itself, so it pastes animated into Files, a chat or a web page. A screenshot is still copied as a picture

description.p: The cards step aside, and the editor learns to lock.

ul.li: The capture cards leave the corner while you choose an area, so they are neither in the way nor in the picture, and come back when you have chosen
A picture pasted into the editor is picked up by its edge, so you can draw on it, and reach what is drawn on it, like anywhere else
Right-click anything in the editor to lock it: a click then goes through it until you right-click it again and unlock it

description.p: Two fixes in how the app keeps its GNOME Shell extension.

ul.li: Started while the screen is locked, the app no longer asks you to log out to finish setting up: GNOME Shell turns the extension off for the lock, and on again at the unlock
An update of the extension that changes more than its code is written as you log out, so it cannot break the extension that runs until then

description.p: The app installs its own GNOME Shell extension.

ul.li: Install, in the welcome window, puts in place the extension the app carries, where it used to ask extensions.gnome.org, which does not have it
After you log out and back in, the next start turns the extension on
A later release updates the extension it installed, and the next login loads it
Where the computer does not allow extensions installed by users, the welcome window says so, rather than asking for another logout

description.p: Two fixes in the GNOME Shell extension.

ul.li: Copying a large screenshot no longer pauses the desktop while the file is read
A pin leaves nothing of its shadow behind when it closes

description.p: The first release of OctoSnap, for GNOME 50 on Wayland.

ul.li: Area, window and full-screen capture from a keyboard shortcut, into a card in the corner
An annotation editor, pinned screenshots and a history of captures
Scrolling capture, text recognition on your own computer, and GIF recording
Pixel-art pets for the desktop, off unless you turn them on
